evidence: seed-demo-auth-users.usecase.ts: SeedDemoAuthUsersUseCase.seedUser runs identityGateway.createUser, then credentialRepository.save(Credential.create({... mustChangePassword: true})), then authorizationGateway.assignRole, with rollbacks deleteByUserId and deleteUser
seed-super-admin.usecase.ts: SeedSuperAdminUseCase.execute repeats the same three steps and the same rollback calls, labelled 'compensate step 1/2'
seed-super-admin.usecase.ts: execute rejects command.password.length < 6; seedUser in seed-demo-auth-users.usecase.ts has no equivalent password check
seed-demo-auth-users.usecase.ts: resetExistingDemoCredential resets existing users; SeedSuperAdminUseCase just returns status 'existing' and changes nothing
seed-demo-auth-users.usecase.ts: execute seeds SystemRoleCode.SUPER_ADMIN with firstName 'Super' / lastName 'Admin', the same as the hard-coded values in SeedSuperAdminUseCase.execute
SeededDemoAuthUser {userId, email, status} and SeedSuperAdminResult {email, status} are near-duplicate result types for the same outcome
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files serve the same concern (seeding auth users), but each one carries its own full copy of the user-provisioning saga, so the same rollback rule lives in two places. The steps are: find the user by email, hash the password, create the identity, save the credential with mustChangePassword true, assign the role, and roll back in reverse order on failure. The copies have already drifted. The super-admin use case checks for a minimum password length of 6; the demo seeder doesn't. The demo seeder resets the credentials of existing users; the super-admin use case doesn't. Only the demo seeder passes phone to createUser. The result types differ too: only SeededDemoAuthUser includes userId. SeedDemoAuthUsersUseCase also seeds a super admin itself instead of reusing SeedSuperAdminUseCase, so the module has two independent ways to create a super admin.

violations.message: SeedSuperAdminUseCase.execute repeats the user-provisioning saga from SeedDemoAuthUsersUseCase.seedUser: create identity, save credential with mustChangePassword, assign role, and roll back in reverse order. It also checks password length inline (< 6), a rule the other seeding path doesn't apply.

SeedDemoAuthUsersUseCase.seedUser has its own copy of the provisioning and rollback flow, and seeds a SUPER_ADMIN itself instead of sharing code with SeedSuperAdminUseCase. The copies already differ: it resets existing users, passes phone, and skips the password check.
